documented_probe: Covering task for C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file) at medium difficulty; verifier fully checks the capability on hidden spec scenarios.
notes: Single-stage: write a spec-driven provisioning tool that declares the mailing lists in the canonical config /etc/keepmsg/lists.conf (lowercase folding, dedup, union merge of duplicate addresses, replacement of the shipped retired lists, idempotency) and save the manager's report. The manager reads ONLY the canonical path; a decoy config sits at /etc/keepmsg.conf and is ignored. Hidden scenarios vary domain and lists, include an empty member set, a merged duplicate address, a zero-list spec (config must exist and describe nothing), and two invalid specs (address outside the domain; member without @) that must exit non-zero with the canonical config unchanged. Distinct from echo-mantle (postfix hashtable on a running cluster) and wren-loom (live TCP daemon + SIGHUP): here the canonical-config loader is an offline reader and the semantics are case-folding/merging/replacement.
